To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) among nursing home residents with dementia, 53,800 (77 %) used at least one drug with anticholinergenic properties (DAP) each month; (2) 67 % of residents with dementia received level 1 DAPs (mild anticholinergic effect), 3 % received level 2 DAPs (moderate anticholinergic), and 31 % received level 3 DAP (severe anticholinergic);

77 % of NH residents with a diagnosis of dementia used DAPs at least once during the 2-year period, 67 % used level 1, 3 %, level 2 and 31 %, level 3, and 13 % of NH resident with dementia used DAP level 2 or 31 and AChEls.
the prevalence of DAp use and concomitantly use of DAP and AChEI among nursing home residents with dementia was high and that the anticholinergenic burden among residents with dementia was also high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of drugs with antimuscarinic properties among nursing home ( NH ) residents with dementia.
a population of patients who are at risk of developing adverse drug events due to anticholinergic drug exposure.
the effects of the use of drugs that have anticholinergic activity (anticholinergics) in older patients with dementia, and the use of drugs with antipsychotic activity in nursing homes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of drugs with antiholinergic properties is common among NH residents with Dementia.
the use of drugs with anticolinergic properties (DAPS) among older adults with dementia may be a significant problem.
DAPs are used in a high proportion of residents with dementia and that a significant proportion of these residents are taking AChEIs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anticholinergic drugs were commonly prescribed for NH residents with dementia and that a substantial proportion of these residents received both anticholinergic and cholinergic medications.
the use of DAPIs among residents with dementia is common and that concomitant use with AChEIs should be discouraged.
the anticholinergenic burden among residents with dementia in NHs is high and may be contributing to cognitive impairment and falls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Dap’s in NH residents with dementia should be avoided or used with caution.

the majority of nursing home residents with dementia use DAPs and that many of these residents also use AChEIs, which may increase their risk of adverse outcomes such as falls and cognitive impairment.
clinicians should consider alternatives with low ACB scores, particularly in patients taking DAPs.
